summary.en: The perfect tense, gender in the past, the future, verb aspect, the conditional and the imperative.
summary.bs: Perfekat, rod u prošlosti, futur, glagolski vid, kondicional i imperativ.

en.one: The perfekat (Croatian: perfekt) is THE past tense in everyday speech: short form of biti + the verb's -o/-la form.
en.explain: Form the participle from the infinitive: drop -ti and add -o (m), -la (f), -lo (n), -li (m pl), -le (f pl), -la (n pl): raditi → radio / radila. Then add sam, si, je, smo, ste, su. 'Radio sam' (I worked, male speaker). Negative: 'Nisam radio.' Question: 'Jesi li radio?' or 'Da li si radio?'
en.example: 'Jučer (juče) sam bila u gradu i kupila sam cipele.' (a woman speaking)
en.why: One past tense covers 'I worked', 'I was working' and 'I have worked'. Simpler than English!
en.mixup: Don't drop the helper verb: say 'On je došao' or 'Došao je', never just 'On došao'. The short form (sam, si, je…) follows the second-position rule (topic 8).

en.one: In the past tense the verb shows the speaker's gender. Men and women say 'I was' differently.
en.explain: A man: 'Bio sam umoran.' A woman: 'Bila sam umorna.' For a group of men or mixed: 'Bili smo.' Only women: 'Bile smo.' For things, it follows the noun's gender: 'Autobus je kasnio.' 'Kuća je bila prazna.' 'Dijete je spavalo.'
en.example: 'Ja sam rođena u Tuzli' (woman) vs 'Ja sam rođen u Tuzli' (man).
en.why: Getting this wrong changes who you are in the sentence, and native speakers notice immediately.
en.mixup: The adjective after biti also agrees: 'Bila sam sretna' (woman), 'Bio sam sretan' (man).

en.one: The future (futur I) is built with the short forms of htjeti (ću, ćeš, će, ćemo, ćete, će) + the infinitive.
en.explain: If the pronoun comes first: 'Ja ću raditi.' If the verb comes first, drop the final -i of the infinitive and write separately: 'Radit ću.' Verbs in -ći stay whole: 'Ići ću.' Negative: neću, nećeš, neće… 'Neću raditi.' Question: 'Hoćeš li doći?' Note: Serbian writes 'radiću' in one word; Bosnian and Croatian write 'radit ću'.
en.example: 'Sutra ću ići kod doktora (liječnika).' 'Hoćeš li doći na rođendan?' – 'Hoću!' / 'Neću.'
en.why: With present, past and future you can already talk about anything in time.
en.mixup: 'ću' can't start a sentence. 'Ću raditi' is wrong; say 'Radit ću' or 'Ja ću raditi'.

en.one: Most verbs come in pairs: imperfective (nesvršeni) for ongoing or repeated actions, perfective (svršeni) for one complete action.
en.explain: pisati / napisati (to write / to write completely), čitati / pročitati, kupovati / kupiti, dolaziti / doći. Imperfective: process, habit, 'was doing'. Perfective: result, done once, finished. Perfective verbs can't express 'right now' in the present: you use them after 'da', 'ako', 'kad' or for the future.
en.example: 'Čitala sam knjigu cijelu večer.' (I was reading – process) vs 'Pročitala sam knjigu.' (I read it through – finished). 'Svaki dan kupujem hljeb (kruh)' vs 'Danas sam kupio hljeb (kruh).'
en.why: Aspect is the Slavic way of saying what English does with tenses like 'was doing' and 'have done'. It's essential for sounding natural.
en.mixup: Don't use a perfective verb for 'I'm doing it now': 'Sada napišem pismo' is wrong. Use 'Sada pišem pismo.'

en.one: The kondicional (would) is built with bih, bi, bi, bismo, biste, bi + the -o/-la participle.
en.explain: 'Ja bih išao (išla).' (I would go.) It's used for wishes, polite requests and hypotheses. The polite form is very common: 'Želio (željela) bih kafu (kavu).' 'Mogli biste mi pomoći?' With 'kad' or 'ako' it makes 'if' sentences: 'Kad bih imao vremena, putovao bih.'
en.example: 'Htjela bih platiti.' (I'd like to pay.) 'Šta (što) bi ti uradio (učinio)?'
en.why: This is the polite form of every request in shops, restaurants and offices.
en.mixup: The forms are fixed: 'ja bih', 'mi bismo'. In casual speech people say 'ja bi' or 'mi bi', but in writing use bih and bismo.

en.one: The imperative gives orders and requests. Take the 'oni' present form, drop the ending, and add -i/-ite or -j/-jte.
en.explain: rade → radi! radite! čitaju → čitaj! čitajte! pišu → piši! pišite! Use the -te form for 'vi' (plural or polite). Negative: ne + imperative, usually with the imperfective verb: 'Ne pušite!' (Don't smoke!). For 'let's': hajde/hajdemo + present: 'Hajdemo kući.'
en.why: Instructions, signs, recipes and polite offers ('Izvolite!') all use the imperative.
en.mixup: 'Izvolite' doesn't mean 'please' in general. It's said when offering or handing something: 'Here you are / Go ahead.'

The conditional (bih) is the polite form.
